**1. Outside view.** The series is heavily smoothed, so week-to-week moves are small: mean absolute WoW change 0.31 over 166 Friday readings. The last 10 weeks show a slow climb from 28.8 (Jul 3) to a plateau at 29.6–29.8 since mid-August: 29.7, 29.8, 29.6, 29.7, 29.7. The last observation (2026-09-04, 29.7) is two releases before the target (2026-09-18), so I need a two-step-ahead forecast. Naive persistence gives 29.7; a momentum extrapolation on the July–August slope (~+0.13/week) would give ~29.95, but the slope has visibly flattened over the last four weeks (net −0.1). Blending: ~29.75–29.85.

**2. Inside view.** Environment is anger-supportive rather than anger-reducing: record diesel/gas prices with an administration fumbling the messaging, "Trump's inflation nation" framing, Cygnal finding anger/disgust/exhaustion dominating the emotional landscape, PPIC showing Californians gloomy about national direction, Trump net approval at −24. None of this is a shock; it's the same slow-burn negativity that produced the summer drift. Worth maybe +0.1 to +0.2 over two weeks. No single discrete event (no war escalation shock, no fiscal cliff) that would produce a step change; the Iran/Hormuz story is normalizing, if anything. Midterm proximity tends to sharpen partisan anger modestly, another +0.05. Against that, the plateau of the last month suggests the model has found a ceiling near 29.7–29.8 and that anger competes with "depressed"/"scared" for the same respondents.

Net: 29.7 + ~0.15 = 29.85, rounding toward 29.8.

**3. Pre-mortem.** Most likely way I'm wrong: I've assumed continuation of a plateau when the series is actually still in a trend and two weeks of +0.2/week takes it to 30.1–30.2, crossing the psychologically notable 30 line; alternatively the summer rise was a bump and it mean-reverts to 29.3–29.4. The second failure mode is real because the 28.8→29.8 run was itself the largest sustained move in months and such runs in MRP trackers often partially retrace. Also, nightly revision means the archived Friday snapshot can differ ~0.1–0.2 from what a clean model run would show. Correction: keep the mean just barely above last value rather than extrapolating the full slope, and widen the sd to cover both a push through 30 and a retrace to 29.3.

**4. Calibrate.** One-week sd for this series is roughly 0.3; two independent-ish steps gives ~0.4, plus trend/regime uncertainty and revision noise → 0.5. That puts one sd at 29.3–30.3, which comfortably contains both a continued climb through 30 and a modest retrace, and matches the observed fact that the series has never moved more than ~0.4 in a single week recently but has moved ~1.0 over ten weeks.

{"mean": 29.8, "sd": 0.5}
